key_insight: Probability-based rewards can become nearly constant on long reasoning traces because the posterior collapses, making verifier-free reinforcement learning unstable and inefficient.
engineering_relevance: For LLM training pipelines, RLCPR improves token efficiency and training stability by filtering concentration-prone samples and penalizing unnecessarily long traces when rewards stop differentiating solutions.
method: Uncertainty-aware data sampling to reduce rollout trajectories likely to suffer posterior concentration.
Concentration-aware regularization to discourage gratuitously long traces when posterior rewards collapse.
Verifier-free RL framework designed for GRPO-style optimization under weak reward signals.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on six of seven benchmarks, with up to 4.0% improvement over the strongest verifier-free RL baseline and better token efficiency.
watch_item: The method depends on detecting posterior concentration reliably, so thresholding and regularization strength may need careful tuning to avoid suppressing useful long-horizon reasoning.
paper_title: Rethinking Probability-Based Reinforcement Learning From Posterior Concentration
